stem: During a one-week 30% off deal, a soundbar's weekly units rose 120%. An analyst quotes -4.0 as the soundbar's long-run elasticity in a pricing review. Why is this risky?

options.text: A short deal pulls sales forward and draws deal seekers, so it overstates the lasting response
Elasticity must be quoted without its sign, so it should be +4.0
It is fine: one week is long enough to measure a lasting price response
An elasticity can never be above 1 in absolute value
